subtitle: From Red Square through Zaryadye to Kitay-gorod

stops.name: State Historical Museum
facts: The State Historical Museum stands at the north-west end of Red Square.
It is responsible for Red Square and Saint Basil's Cathedral within the UNESCO property management framework.
stops.access_info: Museum admission and opening arrangements are set by the State Historical Museum; Red Square itself is a public pedestrian space subject to event and security restrictions.

sources.title: UNESCO Periodic Reporting: Kremlin and Red Square, Moscow

stops.name: Red Square
facts: Red Square lies immediately east of the Kremlin walls.
The Kremlin and Red Square were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1990.
The square links the State Historical Museum, GUM, Lenin's Mausoleum and Saint Basil's Cathedral.
stops.access_info: Public access can be restricted for state ceremonies, events and security operations.

sources.title: UNESCO Periodic Reporting: Kremlin and Red Square, Moscow

stops.name: Saint Basil's Cathedral
facts: The cathedral's formal name is the Cathedral of the Intercession of the Most Holy Theotokos on the Moat.
It was built on the order of Tsar Ivan IV to commemorate victory over the Kazan Khanate.
The surviving stone cathedral was built from 1555 to 1561.
A church over the burial place of Basil the Blessed was added in 1588.
disputed: The names of the builders, Postnik and Barma, come from later sources; the contemporaneous chronicle of the foundation does not name them.
stops.access_info: The cathedral operates as a State Historical Museum site; confirm timed entry and current opening hours before visiting.

sources.title: Saint Basil's Cathedral — State Historical Museum
History of the Intercession Cathedral — State Historical Museum

stops.name: Zaryadye Park Floating Bridge
facts: Zaryadye Park opened on 9 September 2017.
The floating bridge is a boomerang-shaped concrete cantilever more than 140 metres long.
The bridge projects over the Moskva River but does not connect to the opposite bank.
The park was built on the former site of the Rossiya Hotel.
stops.access_info: The bridge is an outdoor public viewpoint; conditions or crowd-control measures may temporarily limit access.

stops.name: Chambers of the Romanov Boyars
facts: The Chambers are a branch of the State Historical Museum.
They are the surviving part of a larger boyar estate.
Their oldest surviving fabric dates to the turn of the 15th and 16th centuries.
The museum interprets the domestic life of Moscow boyars in the 17th century.
legends: Tradition holds that the future first Romanov tsar, Mikhail Fyodorovich, was born on this estate.
disputed: Mikhail Fyodorovich's birth here is presented by official Moscow sources as a tradition rather than a documented certainty.
stops.access_info: Museum: generally open Monday and Wednesday–Sunday; closed Tuesday. Check current hours and tickets before arrival.

sources.title: Chambers of the Romanov Boyars — Discover Moscow
Romanov Dynasty Heritage — Moscow City Web Site

stops.name: Old English Court
facts: In 1556, Ivan IV granted an English trading company a merchant property in Zaryadye that became the English Court.
The site was later called the Old English Court after English merchants received another court near Ilyinsky Gate in 1636.
The chambers were damaged during fighting in Kitay-gorod in 1612 and were subsequently rebuilt.
stops.access_info: A museum site in the former Zaryadye quarter; verify current visitor hours with the State Historical Museum.

sources.title: Mysteries of the Old English Court: Exploring Medieval Moscow

stops.name: Church of the Trinity in Nikitniki
facts: The church was built in the 1630s on land owned by Moscow merchant Grigory Nikitnikov.
It is one of the surviving historic churches in the Kitay-gorod area.
stops.access_info: An active religious site; access to the interior may depend on worship services and church schedules.

stops.name: Kitay-gorod Wall at Varvarka
facts: Kitay-gorod is a historic central area separated from the Kremlin by Red Square.
It was historically defined by its fortifications; only fragments of the wall remain.
Zaryadye is the riverside quarter of historic Kitay-gorod.
stops.access_info: Wall remnants are viewed from public streets; observe barriers and do not climb protected masonry.
